title: Rayfin AMA: Your top questions answered
summary: A Microsoft product-team recap of a Reddit AMA on Rayfin, the developer toolkit for building and deploying Fabric Apps, separating what the tool does today (combining semantic models and Fabric SQL databases in one app, inheriting Fabric row-level security, its own policy-based authorization layer, a recommended backend-secrets pattern) from a long list of features the team describes only as planned or upcoming.
audience: Developers and architects evaluating Rayfin/Fabric Apps for building operational applications on top of Fabric data who need to know which capabilities are usable now versus still on the roadmap.
why_it_matters: Fabric Apps is a new, actively evolving surface area; this post is one of the few product-team statements distinguishing current behavior (e.g. RLS inheritance, the backend-secrets security pattern) from announced-but-not-shipped work (connectors, Functions, expanded auth), which matters for anyone deciding whether to build on it today.
takeaways: Rayfin apps can already combine semantic models for analytics with Fabric SQL databases for operational data in a single application.
When a Rayfin app connects to a semantic model, Fabric's existing row-level security continues to apply, and Rayfin layers its own policy-based authorization on top.
The team's recommended security pattern keeps sensitive data and security logic in the backend, not the frontend.
Most of the roadmap items discussed (external connectors, Functions, TypeScript support, expanded Entra ID/RBAC, more regions) are explicitly described as upcoming, not shipped.
Current guidance is to provision Fabric capacity in West US 2 or North Central US while regional availability expands.

claims.text: Rayfin lets developers build full applications on top of Fabric data that combine semantic models for analytics with Fabric SQL databases for operational data inside a single application experience.
When a Rayfin application connects to a semantic model, Fabric's existing authorization model, including row-level security, continues to be enforced.
Rayfin adds its own policy-based authorization layer on top of Fabric's native security, so an application can combine Fabric-level access control with application-specific access policies.

Microsoft's recommended security pattern for Rayfin applications is to keep sensitive data and security-critical logic out of frontend code, storing protected data and enforcing access rules in managed backend services instead.
Fabric Apps, the application type Rayfin is used to build and deploy, were announced at Microsoft Build.
Microsoft's current guidance, while Rayfin's regional availability is still expanding, is to provision the Fabric capacity used for Rayfin apps in West US 2 or North Central US.

As of this post, most Rayfin capabilities beyond the current semantic-model/SQL-database app pattern (additional data-source connectors, Functions for external API and workflow calls, TypeScript Functions, expanded Entra ID and role-based access control) are described only as planned or upcoming work, not shipped functionality.
